question: Which of the following was one of the last princely states to join the Indian Union?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hyderabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hyderabad** was one of the last princely states to join the Indian Union after independence.
 
• It was ruled by the **Nizam**, who initially wanted to remain independent rather than join India.
 
• Hyderabad posed a significant challenge due to its geographical location as it was surrounded by Indian territories.
 
• The Nizam's refusal to integrate led to the **Operation Polo**, a military operation undertaken by the Indian government.
 
• Operation Polo, also known as the **Police Action**, was carried out in September 1948 to annex Hyderabad into the Indian Union.
 
• It was a swift operation lasting only **five days**, resulting in Hyderabad's integration into India.
 
• The successful annexation of Hyderabad marked the completion of Indian territorial consolidation post-independence.
 
• Hyderabad's integration into the Indian Union was a crucial step for national unity and the establishment of sovereignty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mysore**__

 __
 
• **Mysore** was one of the princely states to join the Indian Union relatively peacefully.
 
• The ruler of Mysore signed the **Instrument of Accession** in 1947, ensuring its integration into India.
 
• Mysore was known for its rich cultural heritage, including the famous **Mysore Palace**.
 
 
 
• **Jodhpur**__
 __
 
• **Jodhpur**, a princely state in Rajasthan, joined the Indian Union in 1947.
 
• The ruler initially showed interest in joining Pakistan but was persuaded to join India due to geographical and political reasons.
 
• Jodhpur is famous for its **Mehrangarh Fort** and vibrant cultural heritage.
 
 
 
• **Travancore**__
 
 
• **Travancore** was one of the princely states in southern India that joined the Indian Union.
 
• The ruler initially resisted but later signed the **Instrument of Accession** after negotiations.
 
• Travancore is renowned for its contributions to art, architecture, and cultural traditions.
